description_short: Select all thermal ALE processes from Fang et al. Table 3 with EPC > 0.5 Å/cycle, returning material, adsorption and removal reactants, EPC, and etching temperature.

paper.title: Thermal atomic layer etching: Mechanism, materials and prospects

tables_modeled.label: Table 3
tables_modeled.description: Summary of thermal ALE processes including etched material, surface-adsorption reactant, surface-removal reactant, etch-per-cycle (EPC), and etching temperature.

comparisons.table_source: Fang et al. (2018), Thermal ALE Table 3

properties_used.label: Material
properties_used.role: Identifies the solid being etched in the thermal ALE process (e.g., SiO2, Al2O3, Si3N4).

properties_used.label: Surface adsorption reactant
properties_used.role: Molecular species responsible for the initial surface modification or adsorption step in the ALE cycle.

properties_used.label: Surface removal reactant
properties_used.role: Reactant that removes the modified surface layer, typically forming volatile products.

properties_used.label: Etch per cycle (EPC)
properties_used.role: Etch-per-cycle value in Å/cycle; used as a proxy for process efficiency and throughput.

properties_used.label: Etching temperature (°C)
properties_used.role: Substrate temperature during the thermal ALE process, relevant for thermal budget and compatibility with underlying materials.

numeric_parsing.strategy: Extract the first numeric token from EPC strings that may contain ranges or multiple values, using a regex capture and casting to xsd:decimal.
numeric_parsing.caveats: For EPC ranges or multi-valued entries, only a single representative number is used; more detailed range-aware analysis would require a dedicated query.

output_shape.description: One row per thermal ALE entry with EPC > 0.5 Å/cycle.
columns: material: label or identifier of the etched material.
surface_adsorption: label or identifier of the surface-adsorption reactant.
surface_removal: label or identifier of the surface-removal reactant.
temp: etching temperature as stored in the comparison (may be literal with units).

postprocessing_notes.interpretation: The filtered list highlights thermal ALE chemistries that combine atomic-scale etching with relatively high EPC, serving as a starting point for comparing process productivity across different materials and reactant pairs.
